heads.la: PRAEFATIO.
heads.en: PREFACE.

heads.la: CAPITULA.
heads.en: CHAPTERS.

heads.la: I.-- De honore ecclesiarum et monasteriorum.
heads.en: I.-- On the honor of churches and monasteries.

heads.la: II.-- De defensoribus ecclesiarum vel monasteriorum.
heads.en: II.-- On the defenders of churches or monasteries.

heads.la: III.-- De ministerio regis.
heads.en: III.-- On the ministry of the king.

heads.la: IV.-- De fidelitate regis.
heads.en: IV.-- On fidelity to the king.

heads.la: V.-- De privilegiis.
heads.en: V.-- On privileges.

heads.la: VI.-- De praeceptis regalibus vel imperialibus.
heads.en: VI.-- On royal or imperial precepts.

heads.la: VII.-- De differentia testamentorum et precariis.
heads.en: VII.-- On the difference between testaments and precaria.

heads.la: VIII.-- De eo quod necessitas excludit leges et canones.
heads.en: VIII.-- On the fact that necessity excludes laws and canons.

heads.la: IX.-- De differentia legis et consuetudinis.
heads.en: IX.-- On the difference between law and custom.

heads.la: X.-- De eo quod sacerdotes mandatum ad gentem extraneam non mittant.
heads.en: X.-- On the fact that priests are not to send a mandate to a foreign people.

heads.la: XI.-- De clericis electis ab aedificatoribus venerabilium locorum, vel haeredibus eorum.
heads.en: XI.-- On clerics chosen by the builders of venerable places, or their heirs.

heads.la: XII.-- De ordinatione vel degradatione presbyterorum.
heads.en: XII.-- On the ordination or degradation of priests.

heads.la: XIII.-- Ut nulla pecunia data episcopi ordinentur.
heads.en: XIII.-- That bishops be ordained with no money given.

heads.la: XIV.-- De electione abbatis.
heads.en: XIV.-- On the election of an abbot.

heads.la: XV.-- De abbatis ordinatione, et de accessu episcopi ad monasterium.
heads.en: XV.-- On the ordination of an abbot, and on the bishop's access to the monastery.

heads.la: XVI.-- De eo quod abbas sacerdos esse debet.
heads.en: XVI.-- On the fact that the abbot ought to be a priest.

heads.la: XVII.-- De accusato abbate quid sit agendum.
heads.en: XVII.-- On what is to be done concerning an accused abbot.

heads.la: XVIII.-- De monachis et sanctimonialibus, ut regulariter vivant.
heads.en: XVIII.-- On monks and nuns, that they live according to rule.

heads.la: XIX.-- De abbate ad regem pertinente.
heads.en: XIX.-- On an abbot belonging to the king.

heads.la: XX.-- De rectore Floriacensi.
heads.en: XX.-- On the ruler of Fleury.

heads.la: XXI.-- De sacerdotio monachi.
heads.en: XXI.-- On the priesthood of a monk.

heads.la: XXII.-- De monachis non servantibus propositum.
heads.en: XXII.-- On monks who do not keep their profession.

heads.la: XXIII.-- De clericis qui monachi volunt fieri, et de insolentia episcoporum in monachos.
heads.en: XXIII.-- On clerics who wish to become monks, and on the insolence of bishops toward monks.

heads.la: XXIV.-- De clericis qui propter vanitatem efficiuntur monachi.
heads.en: XXIV.-- On clerics who become monks out of vanity.

heads.la: XXV.-- De possessionibus ecclesiae.
heads.en: XXV.-- On the possessions of the church.

heads.la: XXVI.-- De monacho, vel sanctimoniali in jus vocata.
heads.en: XXVI.-- On a monk, or a nun, summoned to court.

heads.la: XXVII.-- De his quae a fidelibus in basilicis offeruntur.
heads.en: XXVII.-- On the things that are offered by the faithful in basilicas.

heads.la: XXVIII.-- De episcopis invasoribus praetermissa synodo.
heads.en: XXVIII.-- On bishops who are intruders, a synod having been passed over.

heads.la: XXIX.-- De tricennali praescriptione.
heads.en: XXIX.-- On thirty-year prescription.

heads.la: XXX.-- De dote ecclesiarum.
heads.en: XXX.-- On the endowment of churches.

heads.la: XXXI.-- De episcopo. Quid debeat habere de ecclesia.
heads.en: XXXI.-- On the bishop. What he ought to have from the church.

heads.la: XXXII.-- De rebus ecclesiae, et de proximis fundatorum ejus.
heads.en: XXXII.-- On the property of the church, and on the kinsmen of its founders.

heads.la: XXXIII.-- De provisione suffragii episcoporum.
heads.en: XXXIII.-- On the provision of the bishops' support.

heads.la: XXXIV.-- De indigentia eorum qui res suas contulerunt ecclesiae.
heads.en: XXXIV.-- On the need of those who have bestowed their goods on the church.

heads.la: XXXV.-- De avaritia sacerdotum.
heads.en: XXXV.-- On the avarice of priests.

heads.la: XXXVI.-- De injuste excommunicatis.
heads.en: XXXVI.-- On those unjustly excommunicated.

heads.la: XXXVII.-- De ecclesiis et earum presbyteris.
heads.en: XXXVII.-- On churches and their presbyters.

heads.la: XXXVIII.-- De eo quod episcopus habeat tertiam partem ecclesiae, et potest dare cui voluerit.
heads.en: XXXVIII.-- On the fact that the bishop has a third part of the church, and can give it to whom he will.

heads.la: XXXIX.-- De sanctitate vitae clericorum.
heads.en: XXXIX.-- On holiness of life among clerics.

heads.la: XL.-- De filiis presbyterorum, vel episcoporum, vel diaconorum.
heads.en: XL.-- On the sons of presbyters, or of bishops, or of deacons.

heads.la: XLI.-- De rebus ecclesiae dispensandis.
heads.en: XLI.-- On the stewardship of the property of the church.

heads.la: XLII.-- Ut nullus eligat sibi episcopum successorem.
heads.en: XLII.-- That no one choose for himself a bishop as successor.

heads.la: XLIII.-- De communione.
heads.en: XLIII.-- On communion.

heads.la: XLIV.-- Qualiter sacerdotum accusatores examinandi sint, vel si scriptis inter partes sententia recitata est.
heads.en: XLIV.-- How the accusers of priests are to be examined, or whether the sentence has been read out in writing between the parties.

heads.la: XLV.-- De episcopis in judicium testimonii causa evocatis.
heads.en: XLV.-- On bishops called into court for the sake of testimony.

heads.la: XLVI.-- De accusatis episcopis.
heads.en: XLVI.-- On accused bishops.

heads.la: XLVII.-- De his qui contra episcopum habent causam.
heads.en: XLVII.-- On those who have a case against a bishop.

heads.la: XLVIII.-- De testimoniis clericorum.
heads.en: XLVIII.-- On the testimony of clerics.

heads.la: XLIX.-- Quantum prosit frequens oblatio sacrificii.
heads.en: XLIX.-- How much the frequent offering of the sacrifice profits.

heads.la: L.-- De militantibus.
heads.en: L.-- On soldiers.

heads.la: LI.-- De stipendiis militum.
heads.en: LI.-- On the pay of soldiers.

heads.la: LII.-- De militantibus clericis, et eorum stipendiis.
heads.en: LII.-- On clerics in military service, and their pay.

headnotes.la: …dicit Petro: *Tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam [n: (Matth. XVI, 18)]*. Quia igitur ipsa est oratorium, de quo beatus Pater Benedictus dicit [n: (S. BENEDICT. Reg. cap. 52)]
headnotes.en: … Peter: *Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church [n: (Matth. XVI, 18)]*. Since therefore she is the oratory of which the blessed Father Benedict says [n: (S. BENEDICT. Reg. cap. 52)]

headnotes.la: …entur Christiani intus vel foris violentiam ingerere atriis domus Dei. Unde Theodosius et Valentinianus Augusti, libro nono legum, capitulo 34, Antiocho praeposito [n: (Cod. Theod., lib. IX, tit. 45)]
headnotes.en: …d without, upon the courts of the house of God. Whence Theodosius and Valentinian, the Augusti, in the ninth book of the laws, chapter 34, to Antiochus the prefect [n: (Cod. Theod., lib. IX, tit. 45)]

headnotes.la: … de possessionibus, de redditibus, de oblationibus maximam portionem intercipiunt, quam ecclesiastici capere debuerant. Unde ut talis praesumptio cessaret, ita cautum est in concilio Africano, cap. 64
headnotes.en: …the revenues, from the offerings, the greatest portion, which churchmen ought to have received. Wherefore, that such presumption might cease, provision was made thus in the African council, chapter 64

headnotes.la: …debellare superbos. Unde ex libris, qui ex conciliis sui temporis effecti sunt cum subjectione episcoporum, quanta facile est reperiri, expressum libro II, cap. 1 [n: (Concil. Paris. VI)], post aliqua
headnotes.en: …uncils of their time with the subscription of the bishops — how many such things there are is easy to discover — it is set down in book II, chapter 1 [n: (Concil. Paris. VI)], after some other matters

headnotes.la: …pientia vel vitae merito. Porro ordinatus rex ab omnibus subditis fidem sibi sacramento exigit, ne in aliquibus regni sui finibus discordia generari possit. Hinc habes scriptum in concilio Toletano IV
headnotes.en: …e king, once ordained, exacts fidelity to himself by oath from all his subjects, lest in any parts of his kingdom discord might be engendered. Hence you have it written in the fourth council of Toledo

headnotes.la: …sanctimonialium monasteriis, legem quam semel sub excommunicationis anathemate imposuissent, nunquam, nisi necessitas impediret, deinceps perderent. Unde ita habes scriptum in concilio Nicaeno, cap. 6
headnotes.en: … law which they had once imposed under the anathema of excommunication they should never thereafter lose, unless necessity hindered. Whence you have it thus written in the council of Nicaea, chapter 6
Likewise in the laws, chapter 510

headnotes.la: …m sit vehementior animus, qui nescit servare modum plus aequo anxius. Siquidem non de imperiali praecepto, sed de indiculis epistolarum suarum hoc Carolus proposuit edictum in libro IV capitul. suorum
headnotes.en: …beyond measure, knows not how to keep moderation. Indeed, not concerning an imperial precept, but concerning the brief notes of his letters, Charles set forth this edict in book IV of his capitularies

headnotes.la: …tinentur, aliae sub quotlibet personis censualiter retinentur usu fructuario, aliae per commutationis emphyteosim, id est contractum: quae fit eo modo, quo habetur in libro Conciliorum tertio, cap. 22
headnotes.en: … however many persons, at a rent in usufruct, others by the *emphyteusis* of exchange, that is, a contract: which is made in that manner which is set down in the third book of the Councils, chapter 22

headnotes.la: … quae si publicis utilitatibus non impeditur ipsa pro lege succedit. Nam Cicero in rhetoricis harum similitudinem ac differentiam ita definitione pandere non supersedit [n: (CIC. lib. II, de Invent.)]
headnotes.en: … by public utilities, it succeeds in the place of law. For Cicero, in his rhetorical works, did not forbear to lay open by definition their likeness and difference thus [n: (CIC. lib. II, de Invent.)]

headnotes.la: …Christi communione. Qui vero peccati lege voluntarius rapitur, hunc peccatorum recordatio non tantum contristat quantum delectat: quia ex consensu peccare deliberat. Ac idcirco, sicut Augustinus dicit
headnotes.en: … But he who is willingly carried away by the law of sin — him the remembrance of his sins does not so much sadden as delight, because by consent he deliberates to sin. And therefore, as Augustine says

headnotes.la: …perditi discipuli, panem porrexit; nos vero, peccatorum nostrorum conscii, non ad ostensionem, sed ob commemorationem Christi, Eucharistiam praebeamus fratri. Unde Augustinus [n: (tract. 61 in Joan.)]
headnotes.en: … lost disciple; we, however, conscious of our own sins, should offer the Eucharist to a brother not for a showing forth, but for the commemoration of Christ. Whence Augustine [n: (tract. 61 in Joan.)]
